newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-TIME TO BAN RELEGATION, SAYS HAMBURG COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TIME TO BAN RELEGATION, SAYS HAMBURG COACH.

text.p: Hamburg coach Felix Magath on Thursday suggested a radical reform of the Bundesliga in which play-offs would determine the champions and relegation would become a thing of the past.

The former German international has just returned from Florida where Hamburg prepared for the second half of the Bundesliga season. He was so impressed by the way U.S. sports are organised that he thinks Germany should borrow some ideas.
Play-offs among the top teams would increase excitement and skill-levels, he said.
"We should give spectators more decisive games. When it's almost about life and death, there's more excitement and more quality," Magath told the Hamburger Morgenpost daily.
"The league should be closed, there would be no relegation. That would mean that the fans weren't so aggressive. The hate which comes over now results from fear of relegation."
Magath, a former Hamburg player who scored in their 1983 European Cup triumph over Juventus, said economic factors should determine who were admitted to the league.
He said abolishing relegation would not take the excitement out of the league, as teams would still have to be successful to make money. "Every system has winners and losers."
The Bundesliga consists of 18 teams, with the three bottom clubs being relegated at the end of a season and replaced by the top three from the second division.
